description: The bar chart illustrates the difference in average word error rate (WER) from Whisper large-v3 after applying various cumulative automated optimisation steps, comparing the performance of two models: the NESAC ft model (orange bars) and the SESHA ft model (green bars). The horizontal axis represents the difference in average WER, with values ranging from 0.000 to 0.003, while the vertical axis lists the optimisation steps applied: "Dates," "Americanisms," "Remove Spacing," "Add Spacing," and "Normalised." For each optimisation step, the corresponding bar lengths indicate the WER difference, with numerical values displayed at the end of each bar. The NESAC ft model consistently shows a higher WER difference than the SESHA ft model across all optimisation steps. The largest WER difference is observed for the "Normalised" step, with the NESAC ft model at 0.00334 and the SESHA ft model at 0.00323. The smallest WER difference is for the "Dates" step, with the NESAC ft model at 0.00257 and the SESHA ft model at 0.00228. The chart demonstrates that the SESHA ft model generally performs better (i.e., has a lower WER difference) than the NESAC ft model across all optimisation stages.
